stories.headline: Africa: The 20km Ripple Effect - How Mines Can Trigger Distant Deforestation in Africa
stories.summary: African mines are triggering deforestation beyond their immediate surroundings, with a significant impact up to 20km away. Within one kilometre of a new mine, the local deforestation rate increases by eight percentage points on average compared to unmined areas. Satellite data reveals that each hectare cleared for mining leads to 34 more hectares of forest loss in the surrounding 20km radius. This ripple effect is driven by the construction of roads, settlements, and other infrastructure associated with mining. Africa's rush to supply critical minerals for green energy is a key factor in this hidden deforestation, highlighting the need for sustainable mining practices to mitigate environmental damage. The findings underscore the far-reaching consequences of mining activities on African ecosystems and the importance of considering these impacts in environmental assessments.

stories.headline: Ebola 2026 - Is Nigeria Prepared for Another Crisis?
stories.summary: Nigeria has activated emergency measures to prevent the spread of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, including stricter border screening and health declaration forms. As of May 16, 2026, there were eight laboratory-confirmed cases and 246 suspected cases. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) reports that the country is only 59% prepared for a possible Ebola outbreak. The NCDC Director-General notes that while it's impossible to be 100% prepared, efforts are being made to strengthen preparedness. The African Centre for Disease Control provides weekly updates on the Ebola outbreak response in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. Nigeria's government has tightened entry protocols to detect, investigate, and manage the Bundibugyo virus, aiming to prevent its spread. The country's preparedness is being closely monitored amid the ongoing Ebola threat.

stories.headline: Chinese tycoon Guo Wengui sentenced to 30 years in US prison for fraud
stories.summary: Guo Wengui, a self-exiled Chinese billionaire, has been sentenced to 30 years in prison by a US federal court for defrauding thousands of people out of over $1 billion. The former property tycoon, once believed to be one of China's richest businessmen, fled China and reinvented himself as a dissident. He had close ties to the Trump political circle, including an association with Steve Bannon. Guo's massive financial fraud scheme led to his conviction and subsequent sentencing. The 30-year prison term reflects the severity of the crimes committed, which involved deceiving thousands of individuals out of more than $1 billion. Guo's case has drawn significant attention due to his high-profile connections and the scale of the fraud he perpetrated. He will serve his sentence in a US prison.

stories.headline: PHOTO ESSAY: Two victims on opposite sides of the global scam industry seek to rebuild their lives
stories.summary: Chris Colocousis and Safeer Mohammed Koorimannil are two victims on opposite sides of the global scam industry. An AP/"FRONTLINE" investigation found that American technology is used throughout the digital scam process. Chris, a scam victim, and Safeer, a trafficked individual forced to work in a scam compound, are rebuilding their lives. The investigation revealed that American technology is present in all stages of the global cyberscam industry. Safeer was beaten and forced to assume an online persona, "Ella," while Chris was a target of scams. The two individuals, separated by thousands of miles, represent the contrasting experiences of those affected by the global scam industry. The investigation highlights the widespread use of American technology in facilitating these scams. Both Chris and Safeer are now working to recover and rebuild their lives after their respective ordeals.

stories.headline: Apple accelerates iOS security updates in response to AI risks
stories.summary: Apple is accelerating its iOS security updates in response to the growing risk of AI-powered hacking. The company has released iOS 25.6.2, which patches 30 iPhone bugs, ahead of the planned iOS 26.6 release. This surprise overhaul of its upgrade cycle is driven by concerns that AI can shorten the time from vulnerability disclosure to exploit. Apple has provided direct guidance on the early security content release via its support pages. The updates include security fixes that were originally planned for release with version 26.6. By releasing these fixes earlier, Apple is adapting its risk management to prioritize rapid remediation over waiting for feature releases, forcing shorter intervals between public disclosure and customer patching. This change in approach is expected to impact the operational risk calculus for security teams and mobile developers.

stories.headline: Apple says it is releasing updates early in response to AI cybersecurity concerns
stories.summary: Apple is releasing critical security updates early in response to AI-driven cybersecurity concerns. The updates, which include security fixes for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, were originally planned to be released with version 26.6. However, due to emerging AI cybersecurity threats, Apple has decided to push them out sooner. This move breaks away from the company's traditional practice of bundling security updates with new operating system versions. The early release is intended to address potential vulnerabilities and protect users from evolving AI-powered security risks. The updates are now available, providing users with enhanced security measures to safeguard their devices against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

stories.headline: SteamOS Beta Update Adds dGPU VRAM Management Patch
stories.summary: Valve has released SteamOS Beta update 3.8.20, which includes a patch for managing dGPU VRAM. The patch, developed by Natalie Vock, Maarten Lankhorst, and Maxime Ripard, aims to improve performance and stability on devices with limited VRAM. The update utilizes a VRAM cgroup controller, allowing for fine control over resource allocation and management. This feature enables protection of memory from eviction and sets limits on memory usage. The patch was previously tested and has now been adopted by Valve, bringing improved VRAM management to SteamOS. Additionally, the update includes improvements to Mesa with ray tracing and graphics driver enhancements. The update is expected to greatly improve performance and stability on devices with limited VRAM, such as the Steam Machine. The patch is a result of a collaborative effort to address VRAM management issues on Linux devices.

stories.headline: Newegg slashes price of powerful RTX 5080 gaming PC with Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32GB of DDR5 and 2TB SSD
stories.summary: Newegg has discounted the ABS Eurus Ruby gaming PC from $3,599.99 to $2,599.99. The PC features a Ryzen 7 9800X3D CPU, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 GPU, 32GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 2TB SSD. This configuration makes it a great value for gamers. The build includes Windows 11 Pro and a Gold-rated power supply, along with 360mm liquid cooling. Similar configurations, such as the ABS Kaze II Aqua and Skytech Gaming Azure 3 Plus, also offer high-performance gaming capabilities with the same CPU and GPU. These PCs are equipped with high-speed DDR5 RAM and fast storage options, including 1TB and 2TB SSDs. The discounted price of the ABS Eurus Ruby makes it an attractive option for those seeking a powerful gaming PC.

stories.headline: Morocco to Face Canada in World Cup Round of 16 Morocco is officially going to the Round of 16 after outstanding performance. The Atlas Lions say, Who's next? and the next ones are Canada.
stories.summary: Morocco's national team has secured a spot in the Round of 16 after a historic 2-1 victory over Brazil in the U20 World Cup. This win came after initial doubts following defeats against Japan and Portugal. The team, known as the Atlas Lions, will face Canada in the next round. Morocco's U17 team also qualified for the Round of 16 in the FIFA U17 World Cup after a 16-0 win over New Caledonia. The country is set to make its seventh appearance in the World Cup in 2026, with group stage opponents and schedules already announced. The Atlas Lions' performance has shown significant strength and resilience, overcoming initial setbacks to achieve notable victories and advance in the tournament.

stories.headline: Why is Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi being booed at the World Cup? A French appeals court has confirmed PSG full-back Hakimi will stand trial for rape
stories.summary: Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi is being booed at the World Cup after a French appeals court confirmed he will stand trial for rape. The ruling came hours before Morocco's game against Scotland on June 19. A woman accused Hakimi of raping her at his home in Paris in 2023. The Versailles appeal court found sufficient evidence for the trial to proceed. Despite the controversy, Morocco coach Mohamed Ouahbi expressed support for Hakimi, stating the team is "behind" him and that the player is "very relaxed." Hakimi, a Paris St-Germain defender, will face trial in the rape case, prompting the negative reaction from fans during the World Cup. The trial date has not been announced, but the confirmation of the trial has already impacted Hakimi's reputation and reception at the tournament.

stories.headline: World Cup 2026: The first 4 games in the Round of 32, with penalty shootouts and 3 late goals, have been incredible The Round of 32 is off to a very quick start this summer.
stories.summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup's Round of 32 has begun with exciting matches. Four games have been played, featuring penalty shootouts and late goals. Germany's match ended in a shootout, with José Canale scoring the winning penalty after Kai Havertz missed his attempt. Morocco also won a penalty shootout, defeating the Netherlands 3-2 after the game ended 1-1. Two other matches were decided in stoppage time, showcasing the intense competition in the knockout stage. The Round of 32 will continue until the final 16 teams are determined, with the tournament culminating in the final at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19, 2026. The matches have set a high standard for excitement, with more thrilling games expected in the coming days.

stories.headline: G Kamalini picked in Asian Games squad Yastika Bhatia left out; Shreyanka Patil's selection subject to fitness clearance
stories.summary: India has announced its 15-member squad for the Asian Games 2023, with G Kamalini replacing Yastika Bhatia as the back-up wicketkeeper. This is the only change from the original T20 World Cup squad. Harmanpreet Kaur will continue to lead the team as captain. Kamalini, 17, will serve as the second wicketkeeping option. Additionally, Shreyanka Patil's selection is subject to fitness clearance. The squad has been finalized for the Asian Games, with Kamalini's inclusion marking a new opportunity for the young wicketkeeper-batter. The tournament is set to feature India's women's cricket team competing against other top teams in the region. The squad's composition suggests a focus on maintaining consistency while introducing fresh talent, with Kamalini's selection being a notable development.

stories.headline: ‘Will cut off those hands’: Pakistan minister's threat to India over Indus Waters Treaty
stories.summary: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik has threatened to "cut off those hands" that attempt to control the Indus river system, accusing India of weaponizing water. The warning comes amid escalating tensions between India and Pakistan over the suspended Indus Waters Treaty (IWT). Malik claimed that Pakistan had already declared that anyone trying to deprive it of its water would face severe consequences. The minister's statement was made during a press conference, where he addressed India's decision to keep the decades-old water-sharing pact in abeyance. The IWT has been a source of contention between the two countries, with Pakistan accusing India of violating the treaty's terms. The latest warning from Malik marks a further escalation in rhetoric between the two nations over the disputed treaty. Pakistan has reiterated its commitment to protecting its share of the Indus water.

stories.headline: Refusal to marry long-term live-in partner won’t amount to rape: Chhattisgarh High Court
stories.summary: The Chhattisgarh High Court ruled that refusing to marry a long-term live-in partner does not amount to rape. The court held that a long-term live-in relationship between consenting adults carries a presumption of valid consent. A division bench dismissed an acquittal appeal, upholding the acquittal of a man accused of rape on the pretext of marriage. The court observed that a long-term live-in relationship generally carries a presumption of consent in the physical relationship. It clarified that there is a distinction between rape and consensual sex, and a promise to marry without intention to seduce would not constitute rape. The ruling was delivered by Justices Sanjay S. Agrawal and Narendra Kumar Vyas, setting a precedent that a subsequent refusal to marry in a long-term live-in relationship does not subject a person to prosecution for rape.

stories.headline: AP EAMCET 2026 result OUT today @ cets.apsche.ap.gov.in, check your scorecard here
stories.summary: The AP EAMCET 2026 results have been announced on June 30, 2026, at 11:00 AM by JNTU Kakinada. Students can check their scorecards on the official website, cets.apsche.ap.gov.in. The exam determines eligibility for engineering, agriculture, and pharmacy admissions in Andhra Pradesh. A 75:25 weightage of EAMCET marks and Intermediate results will decide the final ranks. The results include rank details, marks, and subject-wise scores. Students can download their rank cards and scorecards using the direct link provided on the official website. The AP EAMCET 2026 results will also include a toppers list, cutoff updates, and counselling information. Candidates can follow the official website for the latest updates and access to their results, rank cards, and other relevant details. The results are now available for download on the official portal.

stories.headline: Bengaluru physiotherapist found dead, boyfriend unconscious at Karnataka homestay
stories.summary: A 26-year-old physiotherapist from Bengaluru was found dead at a homestay in Karnataka's Chikkaballapur district. Her boyfriend, Mohammed Sanjeet Ali, 26, was discovered unconscious in the same room and hospitalized. The incident occurred at a homestay near Nandi Hills, where the couple was staying. Police suspect that the boyfriend may have attempted suicide after killing the physiotherapist. The room was found locked, and the exact circumstances of the death are being investigated. Police have launched an inquiry into the incident and are gathering evidence to determine the cause of death and the events leading up to it. The victim's body has been sent for autopsy, and the boyfriend is undergoing treatment at a hospital. Further details are awaited as the investigation is ongoing.

stories.headline: The Economic Times] Pacific, the new Gulf: Geopolitics joins petronomics to infuse the region with new energy
stories.summary: The Indo-Pacific region is emerging as a central energy hub due to the US shifting focus from West Asian oil. Ongoing regional tensions and fluctuating prices have driven this change. Geopolitics and petronomics are combining to infuse the region with new energy, earning it the nickname "the new Gulf." The region's growing importance is attributed to its potential to become a major energy supplier, as countries like the US reduce their dependence on West Asian oil. This shift is expected to have significant implications for global energy markets and international relations. The Indo-Pacific region's rise as an energy hub is being closely watched, with countries like India and Japan deepening their economic ties to capitalize on the region's growing energy potential.

stories.headline: US and China Engage in High-Stakes Diplomacy Over Taiwan Strait
stories.summary: The US and China are engaged in high-stakes diplomacy over the Taiwan Strait. The US plans to hold trade talks with Taiwan, potentially undermining China's role as its main trade partner. China has responded with large-scale naval drills and war games near the Taiwan Strait, following Taiwanese President Lai's National Day speech in October 2024. US President Donald Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing for talks aimed at securing economic gains and sustaining a fragile trade truce. China's top diplomat, Wang Yi, warned the US against "plotting" on Taiwan, citing the risk of confrontation. The US has stated its role is to prevent China from using force or coercion to impose its will on Taiwan, without determining the island's future. Tensions between the US, China, and Taiwan remain elevated. Diplomatic efforts are ongoing to manage the situation.

stories.headline: NATO Expands Military Presence in Eastern Europe Amid Russia Tensions
stories.summary: NATO has increased its military presence in Eastern Europe in response to Russia's aggressive actions. The alliance views Russia as the most significant threat to its security and peace in the Euro-Atlantic area. Following a violation of Polish airspace by Russian drones, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte and Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus G. Grynkewich announced the launch of "Eastern Sentry," a military activity to bolster NATO's posture along its eastern flank. Denmark, France, and Germany have joined the mission, with other allies expected to participate later. The Eastern Sentry mission will involve troops and capabilities from several countries to defend the alliance's eastern border with Belarus, Russia, and Ukraine, with new equipment being deployed to enhance NATO's defensive posture.

stories.headline: India and Australia Sign Landmark Defense Pact to Counterbalance China's Influence
stories.summary: India and Australia have signed a landmark defense pact to counterbalance China's influence in the Indo-Pacific region. The agreement was signed during the inaugural bilateral defense ministers' dialogue in Canberra, marking the first visit by an Indian defense minister to Australia since 2013. The pact includes a deal on information sharing, a memorandum of understanding on submarine search and rescue cooperation, and terms of reference on joint staff talks between the two armed forces. The agreement aims to boost defense industry collaboration, increase maritime security cooperation, and promote research on futuristic technology. This move is seen as a strategic step to strengthen ties between the two nations and promote stability in the region, amid growing concerns over China's expanding influence. The deal follows a series of meetings between the defense ministers of the two countries, including a meeting in New Delhi.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Today: Sensex, Nifty down on geopolitical tensions Indian benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, experienced a decline in early trade due to uncertainty surrounding the upcoming US-Iran negotiations in Doha.
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, declined in early trade due to uncertainty surrounding the upcoming US-Iran negotiations in Doha. The BSE Sensex was trading at 76,562.66, down 165.71 points or 0.22%, while the NSE Nifty 50 slipped 65.60 points or 0.27% to 23,880.65. The decline was also attributed to significant foreign fund outflows and a drop in blue-chip IT stocks. This follows a 0.46% decline in the Nifty on Monday. The geopolitical tensions and outflows weighed on market sentiments, leading to a cautious start to trading. The losses in the Sensex and Nifty reflect the uncertainty and volatility in the market, with investors closely watching the developments in the US-Iran negotiations. The market opened lower, extending the previous day's decline, amid concerns over the global geopolitical situation.

stories.headline: Indian Equities Decline for Second Day, IT Sector Drags Market Indian benchmark stock indices, Sensex and Nifty, declined for a second consecutive day, primarily due to selling pressure in IT, oil & gas, and select banking
stories.summary: Indian benchmark stock indices, Sensex and Nifty, declined for a second consecutive day due to selling pressure in the IT, oil & gas, and select banking sectors. The decline follows a trend of market volatility, with the Sensex dipping previously amid escalating tensions between Iran and the US, which led to an increase in oil prices. Recently, the Nifty was at 25,394.25, and the Sensex was at 83,052.44, with the Nifty Smallcap 100 seeing a slight increase. However, the market has been under pressure due to rising geopolitical tensions, particularly the conflict involving Iran, Israel, and the US. The rupee also slipped, and the market witnessed a decline of 142 points in the Sensex. The ongoing tensions and oil price fluctuations continue to impact the Indian equity markets.

stories.headline: Sensex rises over 200 points, Nifty above 24,000; Maruti Suzuki shares jump 3% Indian stock markets rebounded on Tuesday, with both Sensex and Nifty climbing approximately 0.4% after a dip in the previous session.
stories.summary: Indian stock markets rebounded on Tuesday, with the Sensex surging over 200 points to cross 77,000 and the Nifty 50 nearing 24,000, representing a 0.4% climb. The broader market indices, including Midcap and Smallcap, also participated in the upward trend. The BSE Sensex ended at 76,991.22, up 790.54 points or 1.04%, while the Nifty 50 settled at 24,021.65, gaining 197.55 points or 0.83%. Maruti Suzuki shares jumped 3%, contributing to the positive sentiment. The rebound was fueled by factors such as easing geopolitical tensions, falling crude oil prices, and buying in banking and IT stocks. The markets recovered most of the losses from the previous session, boosting investor sentiment.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: Sensex, Nifty Rise As Geopolitical Concerns Ease; Investors Cautious Ahead of Key Talks Stock Market Today: Sensex, Nifty Rise as Geopolitical Concerns Ease; Investors Cautious Ahead of Key Talks, Markets, Times Now
stories.summary: The Indian stock market began Tuesday on a firm note, with the Sensex opening 100 points higher at 77,005.51 and the Nifty marginally higher at 24,032.05. However, both indices declined in early trade as investors remained cautious ahead of crucial US-Iran talks in Doha. The talks, announced by Donald Trump, have sparked caution among investors. The market had snapped a two-session gaining streak on Monday, with the Sensex and Nifty falling up to 0.5% due to fresh escalations in the US-Iran conflict. The Nifty is trading between its 20-day and 100-day exponential moving averages, indicating a lack of clear directional bias. Investor sentiment remains cautious due to mixed global signals and recent technology stock sell-offs, leading to a subdued market opening. The Sensex and Nifty are expected to be influenced by the outcome of the US-Iran talks.

stories.headline: Gold heads for worst month since 2008 as Fed rate-hike bets outweigh safe-haven demand
stories.summary: Gold prices fell over 1% on Tuesday, heading for their worst monthly decline since October 2008. The drop is attributed to expectations of higher US interest rates to curb inflation, outweighing safe-haven demand amid Middle East conflict concerns. A strong dollar is also contributing to gold's decline, making dollar-priced bullion more expensive outside the US. Traders expect three Federal Reserve rate hikes this year, with a 64% chance of a September increase. Gold is traditionally seen as a hedge against inflation, but loses appeal in a high-interest-rate environment. The metal is set for its first quarterly fall since 2024 and the largest since 2013, with silver and platinum also sliding. Analysts cite high inflation, interest rate expectations, and a strong dollar as factors overriding bullish factors for a gold rally.

stories.headline: Cryptos slide as Strategy's bitcoin sales plan pressures market
stories.summary: Major cryptocurrencies have slid in value, with bitcoin falling below $70,000 for the first time since April. The decline is attributed to Strategy's bitcoin sales plan, which has pressured the market. The Japanese yen has also fallen to a 40-year low, boosting the US dollar and impacting risk assets like bitcoin. As a result, bitcoin is now more than 50% below its October 2025 peak, and the wider market has lost roughly $2 trillion. Other cryptocurrencies, including ether, solana, and dogecoin, have also declined. The selloff has affected shares of companies like Strategy and Coinbase, with Strategy's shares down 6% and Coinbase's shares down 5% in early trading following a weekend SEC filing. XRP has held its $1 support despite the market downturn, with rising network activity.

stories.headline: WhatsApp messenger to begin offering usernames
stories.summary: WhatsApp will introduce usernames, allowing users to chat without sharing their phone numbers. The Meta-owned messenger will roll out username reservations worldwide over the coming months, notifying users in each country when available. Creators, small businesses, and organizations can claim WhatsApp usernames already in use on Facebook or Instagram. This update aims to provide an alternative to sharing phone numbers when connecting with others on the platform. The change will be implemented gradually, with users able to reserve unique usernames to use for chatting with family, friends, or businesses. The company announced the update on Monday, marking a significant change to the messaging service used by hundreds of millions of people. Username reservations will be available in each country as the feature is rolled out.

stories.headline: Brompton sells stakes to Decathlon and Chinese Labubu backer
stories.summary: Brompton, a British folding bike manufacturer, has sold stakes to sports retailer Decathlon and Chinese venture capital firm BA Capital. Decathlon has acquired a 10% stake, while BA Capital has purchased a 5% stake, collectively worth approximately £18m. The investment is intended to fund Brompton's expansion into new markets, particularly in France and China, which is the company's largest market. The deal marks a significant development for Brompton as it seeks to grow its global presence. BA Capital is also a backer of Chinese bike-sharing company Labubu. The investment will likely support Brompton's plans to increase its production and distribution capabilities in key markets.

stories.headline: STARTRADER Launches Pre-IPO Trading Products for OpenAI and Anthropic The new CFD instruments give traders early exposure to two of the world's most prominent artificial intelligence companies ahead of anticipated public listings.
stories.summary: STARTRADER, a global multi-asset broker, has launched two new pre-IPO contracts for difference (CFD) products, OPENAIUSD (OpenAI) and ANTHUSD (Anthropic). These instruments provide traders with early exposure to OpenAI and Anthropic, two prominent artificial intelligence companies, ahead of their anticipated public listings. The launch allows traders to speculate on the potential value of these companies before they go public. OpenAI and Anthropic are among the world's most notable AI companies, and the new CFD products offer a unique opportunity for traders to engage with these companies' potential growth. The products are now available on STARTRADER's platform, enabling traders to buy and sell the CFDs in anticipation of the companies' future performance. This move by STARTRADER expands trading options for investors interested in the AI sector.

stories.headline: Google Unveils PaLM 2 AI Model with Improved Performance and Efficiency
stories.summary: Google has unveiled PaLM 2, its latest language model, featuring significant advancements in multilingual support, reasoning abilities, and coding capabilities. This update marks a notable improvement in the company's AI technology, allowing for more efficient and effective understanding and creation of content. PaLM 2 is designed to break new ground in AI capabilities, giving developers more power to build smarter tools and apps. The model has also been adapted for specific applications, such as Med-PaLM 2, an AI tool designed to answer medical questions. This development pushes Google further into the AI race, demonstrating the company's ongoing commitment to evolving its AI technology and providing more advanced tools for developers and users. The unveiling of PaLM 2 highlights the rapid progress being made in the field of artificial intelligence.

stories.headline: Meta Releases Llama AI Model for Research and Development Purposes
stories.summary: Meta has released its Llama 4 AI model for research and development purposes, marking a significant milestone in open-source AI. The Llama 4 model family includes three distinct models, each targeting different use cases, and boasts 10 million token context, 128 mixture-of-experts, and native multimodal support. This release allows developers to download, modify, and deploy the models as they see fit, with some strategic limitations. Llama 4 is designed to perform a range of tasks, including processing and generating text, images, and structured data. The model is optimized for efficiency, reasoning, and real-world deployment, making it a powerful tool for building AI products. With its open-source nature, Llama 4 is changing the way founders approach AI development, offering a unique alternative to proprietary models from other tech giants. The release is seen as a groundbreaking move in the AI industry.

stories.headline: Microsoft Invests in Anthropic AI Startup Focused on Safe and Reliable AI Solutions
stories.summary: Microsoft is investing in Anthropic, an AI startup focused on safe and reliable AI solutions. The investment is part of a larger commitment, with Microsoft planning to invest up to $5 billion in the company. Additionally, Nvidia has pledged up to $10 billion. Anthropic's services will be available on Microsoft Azure, and customers of Microsoft Foundry will have access to Anthropic's Claude models. This investment is part of Microsoft's broader AI strategy, which also includes a $13 billion commitment to OpenAI. Anthropic is growing rapidly, having gone from $87 million to a much larger valuation in a short period. The company is investing heavily in next-generation model development and custom AI infrastructure, driving hyperscaler cloud spending growth in 2026. Anthropic has committed to spending $30 billion on Azure as part of the partnership.
